newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: CRICKET-RAIN WASHES OUT ENGLAND ONE-DAY MATCH.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-RAIN WASHES OUT ENGLAND ONE-DAY MATCH.

text.p: Rain, which blighted the England cricket team's tour of South Africa a year ago, forced the abandonment of the opening match of their first trip to Zimbabwe on Saturday.
A spectacular thunderstorm forced the players off towards
the end of the Zimbabwe Districts XI's innings. Some 65mm of rain fell in an hour, flooding the outfield.
The Districts XI side, containing six test players, had made 198 for nine from 45.3 of their 50 overs when play was abandoned.
"I was glad we fielded and at least had a run around in this heat and altitude," said England coach David Lloyd. "It gave everyone a decent workout at least."
The pick of the English bowlers was Robert Croft with figures of one for 34 from 10 overs. Alan Mullally and Ronnie Irani took three apiece thanks to some good catching.
Debutant Chris Silverwood betrayed nerves on his first appearance for England. The 21-year-old Yorkshire seamer bowled nine wides in a wayward spell.
England play a second one-day match against a President's XI at the Harare Sports Club on Sunday.
